title: Generative AI for Beginners
short_description: A practical, hands-on introduction to generative AI for students, freshers and non-technical professionals. No prior AI experience needed.
description:
Generative AI has gone from a research curiosity to something people use at work every day, and most introductions to it are either marketing or mathematics. This course is neither.

It is built around doing. Roughly seventy per cent of your time is spent with the tools open in front of you: writing prompts, comparing what different models produce, generating images, building a small Python application and finishing with a project you can show someone. The remaining thirty per cent is the concepts you need so the hands-on work makes sense rather than being a sequence of magic incantations.

Fourteen modules take you from what artificial intelligence actually is through prompt engineering, the major AI tools, images, video and audio, coding assistants, ethics, AI agents, retrieval-augmented generation, and a capstone project of your choosing. Every module ends the same way: practice questions with a full answer key, a hands-on lab, and an assignment marked against a published rubric.

The course does not assume you can program. The modules that involve code introduce Python gently, give you starter code, hints and a complete worked solution, and never ask you to write something from a blank page.

Suitable for college students, MBA students, freshers, non-technical professionals and technical learners wanting a practical start

faqs.question: Do I need to know how to code to take this course?
faqs.answer: No. The course is written for people with no programming background, and most modules involve no code at all. The seven modules that do use Python introduce it gradually and give you starter code, hints and a complete worked solution for every exercise, so you are never asked to write something from a blank page.

faqs.question: How long does the course take?
faqs.answer: There is a suggested eight-week plan of a few hours a week, which suits someone fitting it around study or a job. The course is self-paced, so you can move faster or slower. Your progress is saved, so you can stop and come back.

faqs.question: Which AI tools do I need, and do they cost anything?
faqs.answer: The lessons use widely available tools such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Claude, Perplexity and NotebookLM. Each of these has offered a free tier, but features, limits and pricing change often, so check what each tool currently offers before you start a lesson. Where a lesson needs an API key, it uses the smallest amount of usage that demonstrates the idea.

faqs.question: What are the three certification levels?
faqs.answer: Level 1, GenAI Fundamentals, covers modules 1 to 5. Level 2, GenAI Practitioner, covers modules 6 to 13. Level 3, GenAI Project, is awarded for the capstone in module 14. These are completion certificates from this platform recording what you finished here. They are not vendor certifications from OpenAI, Google, Microsoft or Anthropic.

faqs.question: What do I actually build by the end?
faqs.answer: Module 12 has you build and deploy an AI study assistant in Python with a Streamlit interface. Module 13 adds a document question-answering application using retrieval-augmented generation. Module 14 is a capstone you choose from six briefs, which you plan, build and present.

faqs.question: Is this course kept up to date?
faqs.answer: Generative AI tools change quickly. The course teaches the concepts and techniques that stay stable, and deliberately avoids quoting fixed prices, usage limits or feature lists that would be wrong within months. Where a lesson names a tool, it tells you to check the tool's current features for yourself.

faqs.question: Is there a syllabus, and are there cheat sheets?
faqs.answer: Yes. The course reference section contains the full syllabus, a glossary of every term the course introduces, and four cheat sheets covering prompt engineering, image and video prompting, code and APIs, and responsible use. All of them are free to read without enrolling.

faqs.question: How are the certification levels assessed?
faqs.answer: Level 1 and Level 2 each end with an exam: twenty questions plus two applied tasks, marked out of 40 with a pass mark of 28. The Level 1 exam sits at the end of module 5 and the Level 2 exam at the end of module 13. Level 3 is the module 14 capstone, which is a working application, a written evaluation and a ten-minute presentation. The practice questions that close every module are ungraded and are there for you.
